verdict: Apollo reported a $1.1B net loss as Athene's investment book marked down $3.4B in the quarter, overwhelming record fee growth — management fees rose 25% and loan origination hit a record $114B.

kpis.label: Total revenues
kpis.note: -52% vs a year ago, on investment marks

kpis.label: Assets under management
kpis.note: Origination hit a record $114B in the quarter

segments.name: Retirement Services (Athene)
segments.note: Athene's annuity business. Investment income of $5.7B (+14%) was swamped by $3.4B of investment-related losses as markets revalued its portfolio.

segments.name: Asset Management
segments.note: Fees for managing funds and accounts. Management and advisory fees grew strongly, but Apollo's own investment income swung to a $188M loss.

opex.name: Compensation & benefits
opex.note: Pay for Apollo's investment teams — the asset-management business's main cost.

opex.name: Interest expense
opex.note: Interest on Apollo's own corporate debt.

otherDetail: A small net $4M of other income from Apollo's investment activities.

takeaways.title: Athene's portfolio marks drove the loss
takeaways.text: Retirement Services booked $3.4B of investment-related losses (versus a $2.3B gain a year ago) as falling values on its holdings flowed through earnings — even though its underlying investment income grew 14% to $5.7B.

takeaways.title: The fee machine set records
takeaways.text: Management fees rose 25% to $758M and advisory and transaction fees jumped 67% to $633M; origination reached a record $114B in the quarter.

takeaways.title: Scale keeps compounding
takeaways.text: Assets under management reached about $1.07 trillion, and clients entrusted Apollo with $270B of inflows over the last twelve months.

oneTimers: The $3.4B of investment-related losses at Athene are mark-to-market movements on its investment portfolio and related derivatives — they can reverse in later quarters and are excluded from Apollo's preferred 'spread related earnings' measure.
footerNote: Retirement Services' policyholder costs — interest-sensitive contract benefits ($3,669M), future policy benefits ($595M) and acquisition-cost amortization ($476M), net of a $626M market-risk-benefits remeasurement gain — are shown as the cost of revenue. The consolidated net loss was $1,122M; $1,057M was attributable to Apollo common stockholders after noncontrolling interests absorbed $65M of the loss.
